routeSelection.basis: OER Article 10.2 names three specialisations (Philosophy, Politics, Economics) and Article 11.4 requires every student to follow exactly two of them; the normalized target is the generic bachelor and names no specific pair. All three pairings share an identical60ECofYear1common units plus12ECof sharedYear2Practice and an identical Year-3 structure, and combine exactly two disciplines to the same depth (two compulsory courses per chosen specialisation plus four restricted electives, at least one per chosen track), so no pairing is more representative of the programme's broad academic identity, and none is less specialised, than another under the curriculum page, future page or OER Article 10.1's own symmetric description of the three disciplines. The OER's Appendix 1 (Programme overview) prints exactly three annual-plan tables in a fixed order -- 'TRACKS PHILOSOPHY & ECONOMICS', then 'TRACKS PHILOSOPHY & POLITICAL SCIENCE', then 'TRACKS POLITICAL SCIENCE & ECONOMICS' -- so the official-order tie-break selects the first-listed pairing, Philosophy & Economics, fixed before any UCR course was considered and independent of UCR fit.

core: PPE's integrated multidisciplinary identity: examining complex societal problems through combined philosophy, political-science and economics perspectives
Evaluating and constructing solutions to urgent societal challenges using multiple disciplinary lenses together
Ethical reasoning applied to public policy and social choices, and the history of philosophical ideas grounding it
Political science foundations shared by every PPE student regardless of chosen tracks: the state, power, political conflict, and comparative political systems
Microeconomic and macroeconomic foundations shared by every PPE student, and how markets, wellbeing and public choice interact

Philosophy track: compulsory philosophy of science and political philosophy, with restricted ethics/history/global-justice choices; epistemology is an available elective, not selected in this illustration
Economics as a formal Year-2 specialisation: micro/macro-economic methods and policy, behavioural, public and international-trade economics
Formal mathematical, statistical and logical methods -- including decision theory and rigorous argument -- trained across the Methods of PPE sequence
Independent interdisciplinary research culminating in a PPE bachelor thesis
Combining two of PPE's three disciplines in structural depth, as VU's own Year-2 specialisation requires of every student
adjacent: Political institutions, international relations, governance and applied policy as a Politics direction, combined with another PPE discipline
Philosophy and Political Science as the second official pairing: ethical agency, authority, rights and political institutions
questions: How should climate change, migration, AI and international development be governed, and what do economics, political institutions and ethics each contribute to that policy analysis?

What professional and career directions -- policymaking, political leadership, think-tank and policy consulting, journalism and academic research -- does a combined philosophy-politics-economics training prepare graduates for?

alternatives.label: Philosophy & Economics: Ethics, Markets and Public Choice
alternatives.labelReason: Names the actual disciplinary weight and organising question; specialist VU equivalence and recurring integrated applications are not claimed.
alternatives.concept: Ethical agency, emotion and philosophical argument are studied alongside economic models of markets, public policy and decision-making. Five dedicated Philosophy courses and six Economics courses provide sustained substance, supported by political foundations and quantitative and qualitative research. Sociology, rights and communication provide companion perspectives; they do not reproduce VU integrated PPE-in-Practice modules or its compulsory thesis.
progression: Actual workbook offerings and formal prerequisites checked for every placement. BENGATE102 and DISGATE102 precede dependent economics/statistics/mathematics; GOSGATE102 precedes dependent law. PPD is in Year1. Philosophical foundations precede advanced philosophy; comparative politics precedes advanced EU/conflict work. Six or more level3courses are present.

alternatives.labelReason: Names the actual disciplinary weight and organising question; specialist VU equivalence and recurring integrated applications are not claimed.
alternatives.concept: Political institutions, international relations and conflict are studied alongside six Economics courses. This route develops political economy and governance, without claiming to reproduce VU specialist political-science units, integrated applications or thesis.

alternatives.distinctness: The organising question changes disciplinary weight, not just a label. Against ucr-1: 9 exclusive courses (67.5EC) each way. Three qualified responses are supported by sustained disciplinary substance, not general coherence. Primary has five dedicated Philosophy courses37.5EC plus political philosophy7.5 and six Economics courses45EC; theories of ethics, agency and emotion interact with micro/macro, public, behavioural and empirical economic analysis. Second has five Politics courses37.5EC and six Economics45EC, plus WesternPhilosophy/Ethics15EC; international relations, EU institutions, conflict, law and historical context alter the organising priority to institutions and political economy. Third has five Philosophy37.5 and five Politics37.5, rights/constitutional/international law and qualitative/social enquiry; economic foundations remain7.5EC, a stated limitation. This third official pairing can recombine existing courses: rejection merely because no unused catalogue remains was invalid. Each pair differs by at least four courses/30EC; the changed disciplinary weights follow distinct questions, not arbitrary padding. None reproduces VU recurring integrated Practice, specialist philosophy-of-science/history sequence, complete methods trajectory, supervised Tutorial or compulsory individual thesis. These gaps remain substantial and explicit, but UCR actual sustained philosophical, political and economic study materially addresses the target rather than replacing its defining objects with adjacent fields.

Political Philosophy is VU's compulsory Year-2 Philosophy-specialisation unit, distinct from and more advanced than the Year-1 Introduction to Political Philosophy already matched to the shared Political Science: State, Power, Conflict foundation below. UCR's catalogue contains no second, more advanced political-philosophy course, so no counterpart is claimed.
Partial normative authority/state contribution; empirical political-science scope remains broader.
Partial comparative-systems and institutional-change overlap, with empirical political enquiry.
Partial introductory microeconomics; this combined micro/macro course is not counted twice as two complete external units.

Foundations of Macroeconomics is VU's second compulsory Year-1 economics unit. Introduction to Economics, UCR's only introductory economics course, is already matched to Foundations of Microeconomics above and cannot be matched twice; no further UCR counterpart addresses introductory macroeconomics specifically.
Partial consumer/market/behavioural microeconomics overlap; exact external formal methods are not reproduced.
Partial macroeconomic growth, cycles and policy overlap; no full external syllabus equivalence.

International Trade and Development Economics is the fourth Year-2 elective instantiated for the comparator. UCR's catalogue contains no dedicated international-trade or development-economics course; International Macroeconomics above already covers the general macroeconomic-policy territory and is matched to Macro-economics and Policy, so no further counterpart is claimed.
Applied interdisciplinary policy analysis (PPE in Practice)

PPE in Practice I: Wellbeing, Politics and Markets is a broad integrated Year-1 unit combining all three PPE disciplines on a concrete societal theme. UCR's catalogue contains no comparably integrated cross-disciplinary applications course; treating a single-discipline UCR course as a direct substitute would overstate what it actually reproduces, so no counterpart is claimed.
PPE in Practice II: From Theory to Practice is a second broad integrated Year-1 applications unit. For the same reason as PPE in Practice I above, no UCR counterpart is claimed.
Partial qualitative design/interview overlap; the VU political-research and dedicated software trajectory is not identical.
Tutorial PPE is a small-group, supervised academic seminar preparing students for the thesis. UCR's catalogue contains no comparable supervised tutorial/seminar course, so no counterpart is claimed.
Approved study-abroad courses occupy the30ECopen profiling allowance; content remains open, not matched to invented UCR courses.
Compulsory12ECindividual PPE thesis; no scheduled UCR course substitutes. Optional independent research is outside the180ECUCRschedule and is not guaranteed equivalent.
Formal logic does not reproduce philosophy of science.
No exact History of PhilosophyII counterpart established; Philosophy of Mind is a different subject.
VU transaction-cost institutional policy analysis and integrated project are not reproduced by a general law gateway.
Integrated moral, political and economic problem analysis is not reproduced by public international law.
Current VU capstone integrates growth/development models, moral valuation, ecological and catastrophic-risk critiques; UCR level2 environmental movements is a companion topic, not this capstone.

notes.text: These alternatives develop sustained philosophy, politics and economics in different proportions. They do not reproduce VU integrated PPE-in-Practice sequence, specialist philosophy of science and advanced political philosophy, complete methods sequence, supervised Tutorial or compulsory individual thesis. The Philosophy-and-Politics option has only introductory economics. Optional UCR independent research adds study outside the scheduled180EC; it is not a promised substitute for the VU thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Philosophy, Politics and Economics examines social questions through philosophical argument, political analysis and economics. Students study all three disciplines, specialise in two, practise research methods and interdisciplinary application, and complete an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three qualified UCR alternatives emphasise philosophy and economics, political economy and governance, or philosophy and politics. Each develops sustained disciplinary study, with different companion fields. VU integrated applications, specialist units and compulsory supervised thesis remain substantial differences.

curriculum.routeLabel: Philosophy & Economics; selected restricted electives and study abroad
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC illustration selects Ethics II and International Trade in period 4, History of Philosophy II and Global Justice in period 5, qualitative methods and an approved 30 EC study-abroad package. Completing 120 EC in Years 1–2 and 30 EC abroad before the Tutorial and thesis satisfies both published entry thresholds. Approval, attendance, academic-English, progression and thesis-registration rules apply; future course themes and offerings can change.
